failure_modes: Apparent signature loss is caused by direct chemical or physical interference of formulation/excipient components with immuno-capture reagents or detection chemistry (false-positive disruption).
Apparent signature preservation masks underlying EV damage because particle counters register debris or non-membranous particles as unchanged (false-negative disruption).
Insufficient conditioned-medium yield prevents adequately powered (n ≥ 3) matrixed testing, producing non-reproducible or uninterpretable results.
Source-cell lot variability (donor, senescence, clonal drift) or fractionation inconsistency drives between-replicate signal variability, confounding attribution to downstream exposures.

Assay robustness/orthogonality is inadequate: protease/RNase protection or detergent controls do not cleanly distinguish membrane-protected cargo from external or aggregated material, so conclusions about membrane integrity are ambiguous.

Even if an in vitro signature gate is reproducibly defined, it may not predict in vivo recoverability, biodistribution, or functional potency (species- or route-specific barriers), limiting translational value of the gate.

Large-animal/intranasal route-specific behavior (e.g., strong nasal retention and negligible brain uptake) may make any in vitro-identified process gate irrelevant for downstream bridging to clinically meaningful delivery or potency.
Capture-reagent or particle-count instrumentation incompatibility with buffer conditions prevents completion of the required compatibility panels, stalling interpretation and decision-gating.
strongest_objection: The single strongest, bounded reason this proposal could fail is that changes in the orthogonal "intact-EV" analytical signature after downstream exposures will primarily reflect assay interference (capture-reagent incompatibility with formulation components or fractionation artifacts) rather than true loss of membrane integrity or EV association; if so, the qualitative pass/fail gate will be uninformative or misleading because it reports assay artifacts instead of real changes in EV identity or potential function.
